jobs.occupation: Legal Counsel, EMEA Health and Life Sciences (Oracle Health and Life Sciences, Legal) (m/f/d) (Fachanwalt/-anwältin - Medizinrecht)
jobs.description:
At a time when global technological developments and healthcare regulations are occurring and changing at an unprecedented rate, the success of large, complex global organizations that engage deeply in this space requires a legal/business leader who is deeply steeped in the levers, both public and private that impact this industry. To remain competitive in this rapidly changing landscape, organizations require a skilled legal counsel eager to build deeper expertise in healthcare and life sciences regulation, particularly at the EU level.

In this context, we are seeking a German-qualified lawyer with expertise in software as a medical device and healthcare regulatory law, who will support the senior legal team in managing legal and regulatory requirements in the region, especially Germany and the European Union.

About the business

Oracle's Healthcare and Life Sciences business provides industry-specific software and solutions to healthcare providers, payers, pharmaceutical, and medical device companies, and clinical research organizations. It offers a range of products and services, including cloud-based healthcare platforms, data analytics, electronic health records (EHR), and patient engagement systems. The business aims to help organizations improve patient outcomes, lower costs, and accelerate innovation. By leveraging Oracle's technology and expertise, healthcare and life science organizations can streamline their operations, gain insights from data, and make more informed decisions. Oracle also enables secure and compliant handling of sensitive healthcare data, helping organizations meet regulatory requirements and protect patient privacy. With a focus on digital transformation, Oracle's Healthcare and Life Sciences business empowers the industry to embrace modern technologies and improve overall healthcare delivery.

What you’ll do

As Legal Counsel, EMEA Health and Life Sciences, you will support the senior legal team in driving Oracle’s health and life sciences regulatory strategy and implementation in the region, working closely with senior lawyers in the team, the health and medical device regulatory teams and the health and compliance teams, along with product, sales, and consulting teams to provide succinct legal advise on EU and local regulations related to healthcare tech and life sciences products, emphasizing patient safety as a priority.

Specific Responsibilities include:

- Support in developing and implementing the health and life sciences legal regulatory strategy in the region, with a particular focus on Germany and the European Union, support the advise, and education of Oracle Life Sciences and Health staff on legal and regulatory requirements and policy initiatives.
- Support the advise and provide legal drafting, including preparation of legal memoranda and position papers, on legal regulatory issues impacting our customers’ use of Oracle products with a focus on electronic health records technologies, artificial intelligence and machine learning, software as a medical device, and life sciences clinical research.
- Monitor, research, and summarize relevant legal and regulatory developments, especially at the EU and German national level, and assess their impact on Oracle Health and Life Sciences products and services. Provide legal opinions on regulatory questions as required.
- Draft and review legal correspondence with regulatory authorities and courts, and represent Oracle in administrative proceedings as needed, under supervision of senior counsel.
- Assist in the preparation and submission of legal filings with regulatory bodies and agencies in Germany and the European Union to support Oracle’s health policy initiatives.
- Support the implementation of regulatory strategies to help ensure compliance with software as a medical device regulations within Germany and the EU.
- Contribute to projects promoting patient safety and regulatory compliance with guidance from senior legal and product teams.
- Support the review and implementation of regulatory strategies for evolving AI/ML regulations relevant to health and life sciences within the EU, as needed. Additional Responsibilities
- Draft, review, and negotiate commercial agreements, with a focus on legal and regulatory requirements under EU and German law.
- Prepare legal research, detailed memoranda, legal opinions, and comprehensive case files for internal and external stakeholders.
- Support documentation and compliance initiatives related to GDPR, EHDS, and other EU health data regulations.
- Collaborate with internal teams, including product development and compliance, to advise on legal and regulatory implications and progress regulatory program goals.

What you’ll bring

- We are seeking a German qualified lawyer (First and Second State Bar Exam (Volljurist)) with 1–3 years of legal experience in healthcare or life sciences, with a demonstrated background in a law firm, the legal department of a company and/or a regulatory authority.
- Knowledge of healthcare tech and life sciences regulatory requirements in Germany and the EU, including administrative processes.
- Proven experience and interest in Medical Devices / Medical Devices Software and AI Regulation.
- Professional demeanor, confidence, and innovation with the ability to effectively communicate with colleagues and internal stakeholders.
- Excellent writing, analysis, negotiation, and research skills.
- Project management and interpersonal skills.
- Business orientation and ability to balance legal considerations with commercial priorities.
- Ability to perform in a fast-paced and continually evolving business environment.
- Fluency in German and English is required; knowledge of additional EU languages is a plus.

Competencies

- Performance, drive, and execution: You demonstrate initiative and take ownership of your work, consistently meeting deadlines and delivering high-quality results while supporting a culture of accountability. Collaboration You actively contribute to team efforts, value different perspectives, and work effectively with colleagues across departments to help achieve shared objectives.
- Communicating for impact: You communicate clearly and professionally, ensuring transparency and understanding in your work and interactions, and effectively support the organization’s goals.
Competitive edge: You stay informed about industry trends and client needs, identifying opportunities to add value and proposing fresh solutions within your area of responsibility.
- Change agility: You adapt quickly to new tasks, processes, and changing priorities, embracing continuous learning and demonstrating flexibility in a dynamic environment.

Mastering complexity: You approach challenges with a problem-solving mindset, seeking guidance when needed, and contribute to practical solutions for complex issues in your daily tasks. Education First and second German State Bar Exam (or equivalent) is required for this role. Another advanced degree (e.g., Master of Laws or equivalent) is a plus, but not essential.

“At Oracle, we don’t just respect differences—we celebrate them. We believe that innovation starts with inclusion and to create the future we need people with diverse backgrounds, perspectives, and abilities. That’s why we’re committed to creating a workplace where all kinds of people can do their best work. It’s when everyone’s voice is heard and valued that we’re inspired to go beyond what’s been done before. We expressly encourage disabled candidates to apply for this position. jobs.occupation: The Kiel Institute for the World Economy seeks applications for a position as Junior Researcher / Pr (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description:
The Kiel Institute for the World Economy seeks applications for a position as

Junior Researcher / PreDoc (Kiel or Berlin)

We are looking for up to two highly motivated Junior Researchers / PreDocs to join our dynamic research team at the Kiel Institute for the World Economy. The positions are almost full-time (75-90 percent). One position should be based in Kiel and another one optional in Kiel or in our Research Hub in Berlin. Both positions are linked to the research group by Prof. Christoph Trebesch and his ERC project on Great Power Finance.

The two positions have the following focus, respectively:

1. Digital chokepoints: geopolitical risk and telecom networks
2. International capital flows: great powers and cross-border investments across 200 years 

Your Role 

Your main role will be to contribute to cutting-edge research on one or two of the projects. The work will involve extensive data collection and rigorous empirical analysis using historical and contemporary sources. A particular focus of these roles will be archival research and the construction of novel datasets from historical records and documents related to telecommunications, computer science, financial assets and international capital flows.

As part of Christoph Trebesch’s research group, you will work closely with senior researchers on high-impact projects in macroeconomics, economic history, and political economy. The positions offer an excellent opportunity to gain advanced research experience, develop strong empirical skills, and contribute to internationally visible academic work.

Your Profile 

We are looking for a candidate who meets the following criteria:

- ·         Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in economics (completed or close to completion) with very good grades.
- ·         Strong quantitative and empirical skills and experience, particularly:
- For position (1): experience with data on telecommunication and computer science
- For position (2): experience with data on financial assets and/or international capital flows, ideally also historical financial data
- ·         Experience with advanced AI tools and statistical software such as Stata, R, and/or Python.
- ·         Interest in historical research and archival work.
- ·         Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in an international research environment. 
- ·         Excellent analytical and organizational skills, attention to detail, and commitment to high-quality research.
- The working language is English; excellent English skills are therefore required. Some knowledge of German would be useful, but is not important.

We are offering 

The planned contract period is 10 months (starting in the fall of 2026). The salary will be based on the German public sector pay scale at grade EG 12 or 13 TV L. The position is part-time between 75-90%.

The Kiel Institute for the World Economy values diversity. We welcome applications regardless of gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion/belief, disability, age or sexual orientation. The Kiel Institute is an equal opportunity employer with a certified family-friendly policy (https://www.kielinstitut.de/institute/career/equal-opportunity/) . We promote the professional opportunities of women and strongly encourage them to apply. Women with equivalent qualifications, competence and expertise will be given preference. We are committed to employing persons with recognized disabilities and will therefore give them preference over persons without disabilities if they are equally qualified. 

In order to be eligible for this position you have to hold EU citizenship or need to be able to provide a work permit that is valid throughout the time of your contract.

Please submit your application online (https://www.kielinstitut.de/institute/career/job-vacancies/junior-researcher-/-predoc-kiel-or-berlin/) using ID-No. “PreDoc_2026”. Please include (i) a letter of interest, (ii) your CV, (iii) one or two work samples (e.g. Bachelor’s or Master’s thesis), (iv) university transcripts, as well as (if applicable) (v) proofs of relevant work experience. Ideally submit just one PDF, including “PreDoc” and your family name as file name. The deadline for applications is September 7, 2026 Application photos should not be included. 

For additional information, please contact Prof. Christoph Trebesch (christoph.trebesch@kielinstitut.de (https://mailto:christoph.trebesch@kielinstitut.de) ).

Summary

At Apple, we work every single day to craft products that enrich people’s lives. The people here at Apple don’t just create products — they create the kind of wonder that revolutionizes entire industries. We invite you to join our dynamic group, for the unique and rewarding opportunity to contribute to upcoming products that will delight and inspire millions of Apple’s customers every day. Are you interested in doing work that challenges you, expands your thinking, provides innovative solutions for future problems while driving your growth as recognized technical leader in the cellular industry? Apple's RF Transmitter Systems Engineering team is looking for a passionate, talented individual who is eager to break technical boundaries and to change the way of doing things. Our elite team is shaping the mobile market with disruptive RF innovations while taking full responsibility for execution and commitments to schedule and quality. Join our team of leading experts in cellular RF industry and deliver differentiating transmit architectures and solutions for Apple’s wireless products that create amazing value for our customers!

Description

In this role, you will be part of an industry-leading RF Transmitter Systems Engineering team. You will work closely with other architecture- and systems engineering teams, RF design teams and SW teams to assess, specify and drive transmitter concepts with focus on leading-edge performance and uncompromised quality as baseline for differentiating products.

Responsibilities

- Your daily work includes the following tasks: 
- Translate system-level and performance requirements into requirements for the TX line-up and TX features, including RF algorithm specifications for RFICs and system firmware.
- Understand and specify RF algorithms (e.g. power control, calibration) and define the RF control infrastructure, including compute resources, interfaces, memory and timing constraints.
- Research, design, and prototype machine learning models—including neural networks and reinforcement learning—for RF transmitter applications such as power control, calibration, and digital pre-distortion.
- Develop and maintain simulation environments in Python or MATLAB to model RF systems and test AI algorithms.
- Analyze simulation data to evaluate model performance, identify trade-offs, and propose improvements.

Minimum Qualifications

- Proven years of relevant experience in RF, including cellular transmit architectures, or PhD degree with previous work on cellular topics.
- Knowledge of cellular radio/3GPP standards (GSM, UMTS, LTE, LTE-A, 5G NR), including RF aspects as well as system use cases and TX waveforms.
- Familiarity with RF systems and transceiver architecture, including lineup design and component-level trade-offs (e.g. gain, linearity, noise, power, thermal). 
- Solid theoretical grounding and hands-on experience with classical machine learning techniques (e.g., clustering, dimensionality reduction) applied to regression and classification problems.
- Solid theoretical understanding and hands-on experience with neural networks for regression and classification problems. 
- Practical experience across supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.
- Strong analytical skills and the ability to collaborate and communicate across multicultural, global teams.
- BSEE or MSEE.
- Proficiency in English.

Preferred Qualifications

- Initial expertise in transmitter system-level concepts and control procedures like power control, digital predistortion, envelope tracking.
- Background in digital signal processing.
- Understanding of SoC integration constraints and multi-chip RF architectures.
- Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering or equivalent.

jobs.occupation: Scientist (PostDoc) (m/f/d) (100 %) (Elektroniker/in - Geräte und Systeme)
jobs.employer_name: Leibniz-Institut für Agrartechnik und Bioökonomie e.V.
jobs.description:
The Leibniz Institute for Agricultural Engineering and Bioeconomy (ATB) is a pioneer and a driver of bioeconomy research. We create the scientific foundation to transform agricultural, food, industrial and energy systems into a sustainable bio-based circular economy. We develop and integrate techniques, processes and management strategies, effectively converging technologies to intelligently crosslink highly diverse bioeconomic production systems and to control them in a knowledge-based, adaptive and largely automated manner. We conduct research in dialogue with society, policymakers, industry and other stakeholders - knowledge-driven and application-inspired.

As part of the HORIZON project ‘Towards scalable monitoring, reporting, verification and mitigation of non-CO2 greenhouse gas and ammonia emissions from land-based agricultural systems (MARVELA)’, we are looking, subject to funding approval, for a

Scientist (PostDoc) (m/f/d) (100 %)

for the task area 

Development and validation of IoT-based sensor systems for environmental monitoring

Within the MARVELA project, innovative, cost-effective and user-friendly measurement systems for the continuous monitoring of greenhouse gases, ammonia and relevant environmental parameters at farm level will be developed, optimized and validated. At ATB, the work focuses on the further development of modular IoT-based sensor systems, the integration of sensors, embedded electronics and communication interfaces, and their application in livestock buildings and manure-management systems. The developed systems will be tested under laboratory and practical farm conditions and validated against state-of-the-art reference measurement methods.

Your tasks

Your main responsibility will be the development, implementation and scientific validation of electronic measurement systems for agricultural emission monitoring. This includes in particular:

- Further development and optimization of modular IoT-based sensor systems for environmental and emission monitoring
- Integration of sensors, embedded electronics, data loggers, power supplies and communication interfaces into robust measurement systems
- Programming and configuration of microcontrollers, device interfaces and automated data-acquisition systems
- Planning and conducting laboratory tests, calibrations and measurement campaigns in livestock and manure-management systems
- Validation of low-cost and mid-cost sensors against state-of-the-art reference measurement instruments
- Development and implementation of quality-assurance procedures, measurement protocols and technical documentation
- Processing, quality control, statistical analysis and interpretation of measurement data
- Coordination of technical activities with project partners and preparation of scientific publications, reports and presentations

Your qualifications

- Successfully completed doctorate in electrical engineering, mechatronics, technical informatics, embedded systems, measurement and sensor technology, physical engineering or a comparable discipline
- Proven experience in scientific project management
- Proven experience in the development, integration and operation of measurement and sensor systems
- Experience with embedded systems, microcontrollers and hardware-related programming
- Knowledge of common device interfaces and communication protocols, such as I²C, SPI, UART, RS-485, Modbus, Ethernet or LoRaWAN
- Experience in sensor calibration, measurement-system validation, quality assurance and systematic troubleshooting
- Strong programming and data-analysis skills, preferably in Python, R, MATLAB, C or C++
- Very good English skills, an independent and solution-oriented working style, teamwork, willingness to conduct field measurements
- Desirable: Good command of German, EU driving licence class B

We offer

- An attractive, interdisciplinary and international working environment with a highly motivated team
- An exciting position in a cutting-edge field of environmental monitoring and sensor technology
- Excellent infrastructure with state-of-the-art laboratory and measurement technology
- Access to national and international networks for your scientific development
- Training and further education opportunities
- Family-friendly working conditions to promote work-life balance
- Financial contribution to VBB company ticket or Deutschlandticket
- A workplace at the edge of a picturesque landscape, easily accessible by bike or public transport

The full-time position (40 hours/week) is initially limited to 3 years. Part-time employment is also possible if desired. Salary will be based on your qualifications and experience according to TV-L up to pay grade 13. The preferred starting date is in Q1 2027.

For more information, please contact Dr.-Ing. David Janke (Tel.: +49 331-5699 513) and on the Internet at www.atb-potsdam.de (http://www.atb-potsdam.de) .

Have we sparked your interest? Then apply by 25 September 2026 with your cover letter, CV (without photo), and employment references and/or contact details of referees via our online application portal for this job posting (reference number 2026-SM-3) at https://www.atb-potsdam.de/en/career/vacancies (https://www.atb-potsdam.de/en/career/vacancies) . Applications received after the application deadline cannot be considered. We look forward to your application!

Interviews are scheduled to take place in weeks 41 and 42.

We are committed to equal opportunities. Applications from severely disabled candidates will be given preference if equally qualified.

By submitting your application, you agree that your documents may be stored for up to six months even in the case of an unsuccessful application. Further information on data protection can be found here:
https://www.atb-potsdam.de/en/data-protection-declaration-for-the-application-process (https://www.atb-potsdam.de/en/data-protection-declaration-for-the-application-process)

jobs.occupation: Programme & Community Developer (Community-Manager/in)
jobs.description:
Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:
Facilitation; Productowner

Stellenbeschreibung:
Programme & Community Developer Berlin · 32–36 hrs/week · Starting September/October 2026 or by arrangement · fixed on-site times: 3–4 evenings + 1 weekend day

⚠️ Important – please read first: This position is funded exclusively through § 16e SGB II. You can only apply if you meet this funding requirement: **at least 21 of the last 24 months receiving Jobcenter benefits (Bürgergeld/SGB II).**Please note: time with the Agentur für Arbeit (unemployment benefit / Arbeitslosengeld I) does NOT count – only benefits received through the Jobcenter count. If you're unsure whether you qualify, it's best to check quickly with your Jobcenter contact before applying.

About ForEveryone ForEveryone is a non-profit social enterprise in Berlin. We bring people from different backgrounds together, among other things through our community café at Boxhagener Platz and through workshops, events and activities for an international Berlin audience. We are growing, and we are currently reshaping our whole range of activities.

What this role is about We are looking for someone to oversee, develop and be present across our whole range of activities – from workshops to events at our community café at Boxhagener Platz (jam sessions, music nights, exhibitions and more). The clear goal: turning individual activities into recurring small communities with their own memberships. Instead of activities we have to market and fill again every time, we want formats people come back to regularly – a knitting club, a sports format, creative combinations, a recurring music night. You drive this: you sense what the community wants, develop formats to match, test them, run them yourself, recruit and support the volunteers who help carry them, and make sure the good ones actually happen and grow.

What you'll do

- Oversee and support the offering. You keep an eye on all running activities – workshops and café events alike – are regularly present on site, and make sure everything runs smoothly, including the operational side in our booking tool (cancellations, refunds, correct details) – a small but important part of the week.
- Develop and test formats and events. You sense what activities the community wants, identify new workshop, event and mini-formats, research trends and seasonal demand (what are others offering, what works in a summer lull?), and honestly test which formats land well enough to sustain, and which don't.
- Build mini-communities with memberships. You develop formats with recurring communities in mind – ones people belong to as members – and take them from first idea to an established, recurring offering.
- Run activities and enable volunteers. You run workshops and events yourself on a regular basis, at a good standard – weekly, sometimes with support from volunteers. You recruit volunteers (including from among participants), onboard them, give them direct feedback, and support them until they can carry a format.
- Guide formats through their phases. For new formats: experiment and learn from feedback. For established ones: set up clean processes, with reliability and scaling in mind.

What you bring

- Experience running workshops, events, groups or community formats, at a quality others can build on.
- A feel for people and communities, and enjoyment in recruiting and supporting volunteers.
- Conceptual strength: you can develop formats, test them, and judge honestly what works.
- Self-direction and ownership – you drive your area like a genuine project lead.
- Fixed on-site times: at least 3–4 evenings per week (around 2–3 hours each, within the 5–10 pm window) plus 1 day at the weekend (Saturday or Sunday, daytime or evening). These are your core working hours. The rest of your time you can arrange flexibly from the office. This on-site presence comes with a lot of creative freedom, but it is also a clear expectation.
- Comfortable with digital tools; German and English are a strong plus for our multilingual community.

What to expect from us

- A role with real room to shape things: you are building something that doesn't exist yet.
- A small, committed team and real closeness to a lively, international community.
- We set the strategic and financial direction (e.g. the membership model) as managing directors; you develop and decide on the formats independently, with our final sign-off.

Terms

- Hours: 32–36 per week
- Start: September/October 2026 or by arrangement
- Pay: €2,400–2,800 gross/month (at 36 hrs)
- Location: Coworking Kiezlab, Berlin · hybrid
